Under normal circumstances, the Fund invests at least 80% of its net assets, plus borrowings for investment purposes, in common stocks of large-capitalization companies. The Adviser uses a bottom-up fundamental approach to select stocks it believes are trading below their intrinsic value, focusing on companies with strong balance sheets, durable free cash flow and shareholder-friendly capital allocation. The Fund may invest up to 15% of its net assets in securities of foreign issuers, including American Depositary Receipts. The Adviser may sell a stock when it reaches its estimated fair value, when the investment thesis has changed or when a better opportunity is identified. An investment in the Fund is not a bank deposit and is not insured or guaranteed by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation or any other government agency. - **Market Risk.** The value of the Fund's shares may fluctuate as stock markets rise and fall. - **Value Investing Risk.** Undervalued stocks may not appreciate to the extent expected or may remain undervalued for long periods. - **Large-Cap Company Risk.** Large companies may be unable to attain the high growth rates of smaller companies and may fall out of favor. - **Sector Risk.** As of the most recent fiscal year end, the Fund had significant exposure to the financials and health care sectors. - **Foreign Securities Risk.** Foreign investments involve currency, political and liquidity risks. - **Management Risk.** The Adviser's judgments about the attractiveness of securities may prove to be incorrect. The minimum initial investment is $2,500 for Class A and Class C shares ($1,000 for IRAs) and $1,000,000 for Institutional Class shares. The minimum subsequent investment is $100. You may purchase or redeem shares on any day the New York Stock Exchange is open, by mail, by telephone at 1-800-555-0178, through a financial intermediary or by wire. Redemption requests are priced at the net asset value next calculated after receipt in good order. The Fund's distributions are taxable as ordinary income or capital gains, unless you are investing through a tax-deferred arrangement such as a 401(k) plan or an individual retirement account. Withdrawals from tax-deferred accounts may be taxable. If you purchase the Fund through a broker-dealer or other financial intermediary, the Fund and its related companies may pay the intermediary for the sale of Fund shares and related services. These payments may create a conflict of interest by influencing the broker-dealer or other intermediary and your salesperson to recommend the Fund over another investment.
